rationale: Objective peak_allocated_bytes on the current accepted version measures 203,099,136 B (previous-feedback project_measurement candidate_values, both AB/BA endpoints, zero noise). That peak decomposes exactly as live FP32 params 46,758,048 + GPU-resident input 19,267,584 + retained cudnn workspace 8,622,944 + 5 x 25,690,112 = 128,450,560, where 25,690,112 is one 32x64x56x56 FP32 activation. Tensors of that shape exist only in encoder stage 0 (model.resnet.encoder.stages.0: two ResNetBasicLayers at 64ch/56x56) and its input (the stem output), so the binding memory tier is stage 0's full-batch activation coexistence, not the already-optimized stem: parameter search showed stem chunk 4 and 8 both measure exactly 203,099,136 (stem not binding), while chunk 16 rises to 205,196,288 (stem-limited), and per aten::add_/relu/batch_norm evidence in calls.json stage 0 runs out-of-place conv->bn chains plus out-of-place post-add nn.ReLU(inplace=False) around an in-place residual add. The accepted stem micro-batch is verified executing in the current revision (trace: embedder convolution/normalization/activation/max_pool2d n=4, 8 slice.Tensor, empty+copy_ assembly; coverage route stem_microbatch_rows8 with reference invocations 8/8), so a stage-0 edit composes on top of it and the stem tier (~151.7 MB) becomes the post-edit floor. Selection: region scope replacing the stages.0 module boundary (call 595c8331c60823c132ca3a4a) with the same proven pattern - run the unchanged two BasicLayer parents (f3ec7e68beb5e3d3f846d2fa, dfb96bb329e6c3859d690b9a) through context.references on contiguous row chunks of the frozen batch-32 input and assemble chunk results into one [32,64,56,56] tensor for the untouched later stages; no functional dispatch sites, so the legacy direct-callable backend applies. All 72 observed calls in the stages.0 subtree are affected (module, aten and record_function hook invocation counts change 1->4); four stages.1-family calls (47f42cfd2d55620ecd13e733, b92e9ace8737abe290b03c62, ae6782daa6589784cea3aad8, 6d17e25a4f8679b7b8f3d445) are included only because current group families share ownership across stages.0/stages.1; their own execution is unchanged. No call outside this region changes: stem, pooler, classifier and stages.1-3 run exactly as in the accepted version.
hypothesis: Micro-batching stage 0 into 4 chunks of 8 rows lowers peak_allocated_bytes from 203,099,136 B to approximately 151.7 MB (-25%): with batch-8 chunks the stage-0 moment becomes stem output 25,690,112 + assembled stage-0 output 25,690,112 + chunk transients 4 x 6,422,528 = 3 x 25,690,112 total coexistence, matching the tier the unchanged stem (input 19,267,584 + output 25,690,112 + 2 chunk transients) and unchanged stage 1 (stage-0 output 25,690,112 + 4 x 12,845,056) already set at ~151,718,912 B. One 25,690,112 term in the current peak (5 vs the 4 coexisting activations visible in the aten call sequence) is not fully explained by static call-shape analysis, so the honest pessimistic bound is 177,409,024 B (-12.7%); the 4-vs-8-chunk stem equivalence shows such tier plateaus are real and measurable. Throughput: ~0.5 ms headroom exists (accepted version 3.92-3.96 ms, 8079-8121 img/s vs floor 7158.9 = 4.47 ms); stem chunking at batch 8 measured faster than baseline, and stage 0 adds ~54 launches of already-warmed kernels, so images_per_second >= 7158.9 is expected to hold, with a chunk_rows=16 variant inside the same boundary (~177.4 MB peak) as fallback. Numerics: identical aten kernels on contiguous batch slices; eval BatchNorm, out-of-place ReLU and the in-place residual add are per-sample exact, so logits stay within atol=rtol=1e-4 and top-1 stays exact, as the accepted stem micro-batch already demonstrated (max_abs_error 0.0). These benefit, throughput and numerics expectations are hypotheses to be tested by the evaluator's clean timing, peak and quality checks.
